extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users: Principal Investigators (PIs/PDs), Signing Officials (SOs), and institutional grant administrators working with NIH grant closeout, JIT, prior approval, and RPPR workflows
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for preparing/submitting Final RPPRs, responding to FRAM requests, uploading/submitting Just-in-Time (JIT) materials, requesting No-Cost Extensions (NCE), and managing Prior Approval ($500K requests, withdrawals, routing/recall) within the eRA Commons system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim/Final RPPR differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences between Interim/Final RPPR and the annual RPPR are few:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Interim/Final RPPR, only Section D.1 is required in the Participants section; Sections F: Changes and Section H: Budget are not part of the Interim/Final RPPR; Section I: Outcomes is new and Section I is required for both the Interim/Final RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR submission workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps to create and submit the Final RPPR via Closeout Status and Final RPPR Menu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Requires Closeout link for the grant → Process Final RPPR → Initiate to create Final RPPR → Edit to open sections → Complete each required section → use the action buttons (Edit, Check for Errors and Warnings, View, Route, Recall, Submit). See 'How to Do I Fill Out the RPPR Forms' for field-level help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save frequently when editing Final RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to click SAVE when moving between sections or unsaved data may be lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click Save between sections; when done, click Cancel to return to Final RPPR Menu. Unsaved data can be lost if Save is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR action buttons available
rubrics_metrics.description: Final RPPR Menu screen provides several action buttons at the bottom to complete the Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available actions include Editing the RPPR Forms, Checking for Errors and Warnings, Viewing the RPPR, Routing the RPPR, Recalling the RPPR, and Submitting RPPR to Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR requirement at closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) is required for any grant that has ended and any grant that is not to be extended through award of a new competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare in accordance with instructions provided by the awarding component; refer to 'Submitting Your Final Research Performance Progress Report' for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM request and notification process
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Program Official (PO) requires additional materials during Final RPPR review, they will submit a FRAM request and the PI is notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI receives email and Closeout Status updates to FRAM Requested; a FRAM Update link appears in Closeout Status as an action on the Final RPPR line item. If the FRAM Update link is not present, the request was not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI responsibility to upload FRAM attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the PI who is responsible for uploading requested FRAM via the Closeout module in Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Closeout Status select the FRAM Update link → use Add Attachment to select the document from the local computer → the attached document must pass system validations before being appended.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM attachment format and size requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: FRAM attachments must be in PDF format and no larger than 6MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Add Attachment; after passing system validations the screen shows 'FRAM was successfully uploaded and is ready for processing by the SO in your institution.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing, deleting, and appending FRAM attachments before SO submission
rubrics_metrics.description: FRAM attachments can be viewed at any time and deleted before submission to Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View Attachment or View buttons allow previewing; Delete Attachment button removes attachments prior to SO submission. Subsequent uploads are appended in the stored PDF viewable in Status Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: SO submits FRAM to Agency; SO-only role
rubrics_metrics.description: Once FRAM is uploaded by the PI, only those with an SO role in Commons can submit FRAM to Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO selects FRAM Update link → optional View Attachment → Submit → must confirm certification by selecting I Agree → after successful submission the Closeout Status shows FRAM Submitted By <SO Name> and FRAM Update link replaced by View FRAM; FRAM cannot be edited after submission to Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM post-submission behavior and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: After SO submission Commons sends notifications and aggregates documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email notifications are sent to the SO who submitted and to the PI; a separate notification is sent to the PO. Commons generates a PDF containing all FRAM documents accessible in Status Information under Other Relevant Documents. PO may rescind approval and make FRAM Update link available again. SOs can continue to add attachments after submission (before acceptance of the FPR); subsequent documents are added to the generated PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: JIT allows electronic submittal of additional grant application information after peer review and prior to funding, when requested by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit JIT information until specifically requested by the agency (eRA-system emails or direct PO contact). JIT becomes available generally for applications within certain percentile or priority score ranges; check policy and FOA criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may upload and who may submit JIT
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs (or delegates) may upload and save JIT attachments; only an SO can submit the JIT to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs can upload and save but must have an SO submit. SO role must be used to submit; Commons performs validations on save and submission and will show error messages for missing required info.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT attachment types and format/size
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed JIT upload file types include Other Support File, Budget Upload, Other Upload, Human Subject Education, Genome Data Sharing Certification; attachments should be PDF and maximum size 6MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other Support is always available; use the specified upload/import buttons or drag-and-drop. Uploaded file displays name and upload date and a confirmation message upon successful save.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support content definition for JIT
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Support should include active and pending support for all key personnel — all financial resources supporting an individual's research (federal, non-federal, commercial, institutional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training awards, prizes, or gifts do not need to be included. Follow the suggested format available at the referenced othersupport.doc and upload accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT IRB/IACUC verification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If application involves vertebrate animals or human subjects, verification of the date of IACUC or IRB approval is required on the JIT screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter IRB Date and Assurance Number as appropriate; save to allow SO submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT save/validation and submission behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Saving JIT performs system validations and displays error messages for missing required information; SOs see Submit enabled after save.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Save a confirmation message indicates information was saved and that a user with required authority must still submit. SOs may view the Just In Time Report before submitting; submit triggers Applicant and Organization Certification and Acceptance pop-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT resubmission and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: You can resubmit JIT information as many times as necessary; each JIT section can be submitted separately and more than once as long as at least one field element has been completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Just In Time screen displays the Number of Submissions for each piece of information. Status result screens display the JIT link with the number of times revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Cost Extension (NCE) one-time policy and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH standard terms allow grantees to extend the final budget period one time for up to 12 months without additional NIH funds, taken before the project period ends, with required NIH notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are permitted only if no additional funds required and no change in the project's originally approved scope. A mandatory justification must fit one of: (a) additional time required to complete approved project, (b) ensure continuity while a competing continuation is under review, or (c) permit orderly phase-out of a project not receiving continued support. Remaining funds alone is not sufficient justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCE process via Commons (timing, increments, SO role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commons No-Cost Extension feature allows SO users to request NCE in one-month increments up to 12 months; the link is available 90 days before project end and removed at midnight on the project end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH requires grantees to use the NCE feature in Commons; NIH will not accept notification via other channels. To submit: search for grant in Status - General Search → select Extension link → choose months from Extend drop-down (updates 'This will extend the project to' field) → select Extend Project Date → confirm and select Confirm on the confirmation screen. If an internal business error prevents processing, the link displays as Extension Error with instruction to contact appropriate support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications update requirement for NCE
rubrics_metrics.description: In extending the final budget period, the grantee agrees to update all required certifications, including human subjects and animal welfare, in accordance with applicable regulations and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantee must ensure certifications are current when requesting an NCE; additional project period extensions beyond the one-time NCE require prior NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Institution via Relinquishing Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Change of Institution process allows extramural grantee institutions to submit Relinquishing Statements (RS) electronically via Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage Relinquishing Statement and Relinquishing Statement screens are accessible via the Status module. Refer to Commons online help or the Commons Change of Institution User Guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Approval module purpose and access
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prior Approval module allows PIs and SOs to respond to prior approval invitations from the granting agency or to withdraw a successfully submitted grant application that has not yet been awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access via Prior Approval tab on Commons Home screen. PI options include initiating a Withdrawal Request or List My Requests; SOs can initiate Withdrawal, list existing requests, and search for requests. For certain actions (e.g., initiating a $500K request) contact PO as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: List My Requests / Search behavior and views
rubrics_metrics.description: List My Requests displays all Prior Approval Requests for which the PI is the Contact PI; SO view displays Prior Approval Requests in status Pending SO for the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOs should use Search Prior Approval to find requests not in Pending SO. From hitlists users can View PDF, View History, Modify, or View the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search criteria for Prior Approval requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Search Prior Approval Requests screen allows searching by Request ID, Request Type (Withdrawal or 500K), Request Status (Submitted to Agency, In Progress SO, In Progress PI), PI lookup, Activity Code/IC/Serial, and Submission Date Range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter criteria and select Search to obtain a hit list; use Clear Search to reset fields. From results choose available actions in the Actions column.

rubrics_metrics.name: $500K request prior contact and initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants planning to submit an application with $500,000 or more in direct costs in any one budget year must contact their Program Official and obtain agreement six weeks prior to application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO elects to receive the request electronically they will initiate an invitation that opens a request in the Prior Approval module; the option to submit a $500K request is not visible until the PO has initiated the invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: $500K Modify Request required fields (PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Prior Approval Request 500K - Modify Request screen the system pre-populates PI, Organization, IC, and Program Official information; required fields for PI must be populated to continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required fields include Project Title, FOA, Anticipated Submission Date, and Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: $500K Modify Request required fields (SO) and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: On the 500K Modify Request screen SOs must provide Project Title, FOA (Funding Opportunity Announcement Number), Anticipated Submission Date, and a Justification (character limit 500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated Submission Date may not be in the past or more than 120 days in the future. If request is for a Renewal (Type 2), Activity Code and Serial Number of grant family may also be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: All required fields must be populated before $500K submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All required (*) fields must be populated before submission of the $500K request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI may submit or route the request to an SO for final review and submission. Upon successful submission the system sends email notifications to the submitter and associated PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiating and submitting a Withdrawal Request
rubrics_metrics.description: Both PIs and SOs may initiate Withdrawal Requests but only an SO may submit them to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate by selecting Withdrawal Request on Prior Approval landing page → Available Grants hitlist shows eligible grants (PIs see grants where they are contact PI; SOs see institutional grants). Select grant, Initiate Withdrawal Request, add justifications and supporting documents on Modify Request screen, and when ready an SO must submit. Some application statuses (Awarded, Withdrawn, Canceled) will not appear in hitlist. If agency action prevents withdrawal, system instructs to submit to Division of Receipt and Referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify Request capabilities and upload limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify Request screen allows entering/modifying Justification, uploading PDF documents, viewing history, routing, deleting, saving, and canceling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uploaded PDF documents should not exceed 5MB (some limits on number of documents may apply per FOA or PO direction). Users can delete uploaded PDFs before submission. $500K requests cannot be deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged review before Withdrawal submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees are strongly encouraged to review the Withdrawal Request prior to submission to ensure all relevant information and attachments are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only an SO can submit a Withdrawal Request and only when the SO is the current reviewer of the report. After submitting, a notification is sent to the submitting SO and PI(s) that the Withdrawal request has been submitted to Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing Prior Approval Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is In Progress PI, the PI can route it to the SO; if In Progress SO, the SO can route it to the PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To route select Route from the bottom of Modify Request screen → optional comments may be entered for next reviewer → click Route to [SO/PI] button which notifies the recipient. The person who routed the request can no longer edit it; modification is available only to the new reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalling Prior Approval Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously routed Prior Approval Requests can be recalled by the previous reviewer; an SO may recall even if not the last reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once status becomes 'Submitted to Agency' it can no longer be recalled. To recall, select the Recall button from the View Request screen; the request reappears in Modify Request screen and is available to modify, save, route, delete, submit, cancel, or view history.

rubrics_metrics.name: View History functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: View History screen enables users to view progress/history of requests prior to submission (PIs and SOs access via Modify or View Request screens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-submission SOs can search for requests with status Submitted to Agency and click View History; PIs access View History via List My Requests. View History displays actions taken so far and routing progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR module features summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR module supports electronic initiation, routing, error checking, submission, final RPPR creation, and storage of RPPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features include electronic initiation of an RPPR, electronic routing to authorizing officials for review and approval prior to submission to the agency, viewing RPPR routing history, error checking capabilities, electronic submission of RPPR (including Final RPPR), ability for an SO to delegate authority to a PD/PI for submitting an RPPR, and a generated PDF version stored in the electronic grant folder (Commons Status Information screen). A detailed field-by-field instruction guide (NIH RPPR Instruction Guide) is available online.
